what_you_do: You hold a picture of something you feel stuck on in mind while following a moving dot for 8 short rounds, then plan your first step.

method.name: Holding a picture in mind during a demanding task (working-memory taxation)
method.text: Working memory, the mental space for what you're thinking about right now, has limited room. Holding a picture while tracking a moving target makes the two compete for it, so the picture may feel less vivid for a while.

research.text: A lab experiment with 37 students found that recalling a recurring, unpleasant image of a feared future event during an eye-movement task made it less vivid straight afterwards than recall alone. The drop in how upsetting it felt was smaller and unclear.
The kind of task matters: in two lab experiments, a visual game played after a distressing film reduced later intrusive images; a word quiz did not, and once increased them.

about_this_exercise: This is an experimental exercise, and this version hasn't been tested itself. The lab experiment used eye movements, not a moving dot. The planning step uses the method of “Plan your first step”.
limits: Effects were modest and immediate; how long they last is unknown.
It hasn't been shown that a less vivid picture helps anyone start.
Choose an everyday situation, never a painful personal memory.
